transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-07 15:00 PT
Duration: ~49 minutes
Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Diego (Redwood Solutions), Asha (Goldcrest Head of ML), Marcus (Goldcrest CTO), Kimberly (Goldcrest Infra), Jon (Product)

Summary:
Short intake to understand Goldcrest's unit economics needs for a customer-facing assistant. Heavy focus on per-token pricing, batching/caching levers, and whether a hosted pilot will scale or if Dedicated/Private is required for budget/SLA/security. Action: pricing scenarios + benchmark plan + security follow-ups.

Topics:
- Current stack and latency targets
- Expected token volumes & traffic shape (burst vs steady)
- Hosted vs Dedicated unit cost tradeoffs
- Caching (prefix and KV) and batching impact on per-token economics
- Private deployment (VPC/KMS/SOC2) constraints
- Pilot scope and success criteria

Action items (captured in notes): see metadata action_items

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll keep this to about 45 minutes. quick intros?
[00:07] Asha: Hi, Asha, head of ML at Goldcrest. we're evaluating ways to serve an assistant for our analytics product, want to understand cost and performance tradeoffs.
[00:14] Marcus: Marcus here, CTO, mostly concerned about predictable spend and security controls.
[00:18] Kimberly: Kimberly, infra lead, I'll own anything VPC/KMS related.
[00:22] Liam: Liam from Redwood, I do the performance side, happy to dig into batching and kv cache behaviour.
[00:27] Diego: Diego, solutions, I'll follow procurement / pilot scoping.
[00:31] Jon: Jon — product owner, i'll help with the success criteria.

[01:02] Samira: Cool. Asha, can you give a quick picture of expected traffic? daily tokens, percent of chat vs short completions?
[01:12] Asha: Right now rough numbers — early stage but planning for 300k to 1.2M tokens/day within 3 months if the pilot goes well. Most calls are multi-turn chat for analytics queries, so sequences can be long — average 600 tokens per session but tails to 2k. hope to keep 99th pct latency under 300ms for first-party users.

[02:05] Liam: Thanks. that's helpful. two immediate levers we'll look at: batching (amortizes per-request overhead) and caching (prefix + KV cache to avoid recompute). batching increases throughput but can add latency. caching helps a lot for repeated system prompts or common prefixes in analytics queries.

[02:40] Marcus: question — is hosted Redwood able to guarantee the same latency SLOs as Dedicated? or do we need to reserve capacity?
[02:46] Samira: good question. hosted is fast to start — we have multi-tenant pools optimized for low-latency, but if you need strict SLOs and predictable unit price at scale we typically recommend Dedicated. Dedicated also gives you reserved throughput and more consistent queuing behavior, which helps with 99th pct.

[03:10] Asha: Can you quantify the unit price difference? ballpark per-token?
[03:17] Samira: we'll send detailed numbers, but rough framing: hosted per-token is simpler and lower up-front, but can be more variable at very high volume. Dedicated has a committed monthly cost + lower effective per-token when you're utilizing the reserved capacity. For example — on a modeled 1M tokens/day workload with 70% cache-hit and good batching, Dedicated can be 20-45% cheaper per effective output token after amortizing the commit.

[03:48] Kim (Kimberly) (mislabelled as 'Kim'): ok what's the cache hit assumption — 70% seems optimistic for analytics queries because users ask ad-hoc Qs
[03:56] Liam: yeah good point, 70% assumes a lot of repeated system prompts and dashboard-level queries. if your queries are highly unique the KV/prefix cache helps mainly for system messages and the static portions. even a 20-30% prefix cache hit can materially lower tokens sent to the model. and batching helps for throughput especially during concentrated query windows.

[04:35] Marcus: also want to understand the billing model — is it per-input token, per-output token, both?
[04:41] Samira: Redwood's hosted billing is typically per-input+output tokens, with extra for embeddings or special services. for Dedicated we can model your unit economics as cost per effective output token factoring in cache hits, batching, and quantization choices. we'll provide a per-call example in the pricing deck.

[05:10] Jon: what's quantization impact? we have some regulatory requirements but are ok with minor quality delta if it drops cost.
[05:18] Liam: quantization—moving from FP16 to 4-bit/INT8 can reduce memory and increase throughput; latency can improve and unit cost drops. there's a small quality delta in some tasks; we'll recommend model variants and run evals on your prompt sets. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization profiles per-workload.

[05:54] Asha: can we run a benchmark with our prompts and see signal-to-noise?
[05:58] Diego: yes that's the plan for the pilot we propose: 2 weeks of synthetic traffic + a 48-hr real traffic window. liability: we need a way to reproduce tails and burst patterns.

[06:30] Kimberly: on private deployments: if we go VPC or on-prem, what changes? KMS requirements — we use Cloud HSM, want key separation — can Redwood integrate with customer-managed KMS?
[06:40] Samira: yes — for Private we support customer-managed KMS integrations and an on-prem package. VPC private control plane means we still run the runtime but you control the network and keys. audit logs and SOC2 artifacts are available. some customers choose Private for data residency and full compliance.

[07:05] Marcus: what's the procurement timeline typically? we need legal to see SOC2, contracts, and a data processing addendum — do you have those ready?
[07:11] Diego: we do. i'll attach SOC2, privacy + DPA and a private deployment checklist after this call.

[07:26] Asha: back to unit econ — can you give a worked example? say 1M tokens/day, cache hit 30%, batching reduces per-request overhead by 25% — what's the delta hosted vs dedicated?
[07:36] Liam: without the full model of your prompts it's illustrative only, but with 30% cache + moderate batching you might see hosted effective unit cost X, and Dedicated could be 15-30% cheaper once you hit commit thresholds. the real lever is utilization of the Dedicated pool; if you only run bursts and low utilization, Dedicated can be more expensive. we typically run sensitivity models across utilization and cache hit rates.

[08:15] Asha: how do fallbacks work if capacity is constrained or a model update regresses quality?
[08:20] Samira: Redwood's routing supports automatic fallbacks to compatible model variants and regions. rollouts can be canaryed and A/B'd. we also have quality regressions tied to prompt evals — we alert if a new model shows a downward quality trend on your eval set.

[09:02] Marcus: what about multi-tenant data leakage concerns? our legal team will push back on any co-mingling.
[09:09] Samira: Dedicated provides stronger isolation: reserved GPUs and tenancy separation. Private (VPC/on-prem) is the strongest for regulatory needs. we can also provide isolation contracts and technical attestations.

[09:45] Jon: circling back to pilot scope — what do you need from us to run a meaningful benchmark?
[09:51] Liam: three things: representative prompt set (2-5k prompts), traffic profile (burst patterns and concurrency), and success metrics (latency percentiles, cost per effective query, quality thresholds). with that we can run both hosted and a Dedicated simulator to compare.

[10:17] Asha: can Redwood simulate the KV cache hit distribution? some of our queries are dynamic, but dashboards have repeated prefixes for filter prompts.
[10:26] Liam: yes, we'll instrument the runner to emulate prefix hits and KV reuse. sometimes transcription will render KV as 'K V' — just to note the runner cares about exact prefix matching.

[11:05] Kimberly: network — if we do VPC peering for Private, what bandwidth needs should we expect? we have heavy telemetry and want to avoid bottlenecks.
[11:13] Diego: typical per-request payloads are small, but KV/cache state sync and model shards matter. we'll share recommended sizing for peak qps and a small diagram for peering.

[12:04] Marcus: one more on pricing: what about burst credits or burst capacity? sometimes we have unpredictable spikes — how does Redwood handle that without huge overcommit?
[12:12] Samira: Hosted has elastic autoscaling but it can be pricier at large spikes. Dedicated has burst capacity options you can configure — commit for baseline and allow bursts with an overage rate. we can model expected overage spend in the pricing scenarios.

[12:45] Asha: do you support token-level cost breakdowns and per-route dashboards? our product team needs to instrument cost per feature.

[12:51] Diego: yes, Redwood Console provides token-level breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and tracing hooks so you can attribute cost back to product features.

[13:12] Jon: ok good. also curious if Redwood can provide guidance on model selection — like smaller Llama or larger models for more compositional question answering — which changes token patterns.

[13:20] Liam: absolutely. model selection is workload dependent. sometimes a smaller specialized model with retrieval and reranking is cheaper than a large general model. Redwood Optimize can recommend model+quantization combos for cost/latency.

[14:01] Marcus: anything else on compliance? we need ISO and SOC2 reports, and specific audit logs for data access. can you provide evidence?
[14:07] Diego: yes i'll attach SOC2 type II and the audit log schema. for Private we can ship additional logs and integrate with your SIEM.

[15:00] Asha: skimming the tradeoffs, we need a clear POC that shows 1) cost per effective query 2) latency tails 3) quality baseline.

[15:08] Samira: agreed. proposed pilot: 2 weeks hosted run with synthetic traffic and a 48hr window of real users, run the same set on a Dedicated simulator to show committed vs pay-as-you-go economics. Redwood provides the runner, you provide prompts and SLOs.

[15:28] Marcus: budget — how should we budget for the pilot? we have a constrained budget and would like an upper bound.

[15:34] Samira: we'll provide two scenarios: conservative (assume low cache & poor batching) and optimistic (good cache, batching, quantization). each will show expected spend and a recommended committed tier for Dedicated if it makes sense.

[16:01] Kimberly: security deep dive — let's tentatively schedule post-pricing call next Thursday, I'll invite network/security.

[16:08] Diego: noted. we'll include a technical checklist in the follow-up.

[16:20] Asha: small nit: do you support per-tenant RBAC inside a Dedicated deployment? we have multiple internal teams.

[16:27] Liam: yes, RBAC and token-level controls are available in the Console, and we can set up per-route quotas.

[17:00] Jon: can you include a worked example of how caching changes effective tokens? numbers help the exec team.

[17:09] Samira: we'll add a worked example in the pricing deck, with sensitivity to cache-hit, batch size, and quantization.

[17:40] Asha: great. any objections from anyone?
[17:45] Marcus: no, just want the SOC2 and DPA sent.

[17:52] Kimberly: no objections, want the VPC diagram and network requirements.

[18:00] Samira: cool. recap: we'll send pricing scenarios, pilot plan, SOC2 + security checklist, and schedule the VPC deep-dive. next call? how about Tue 2026-08-11?

[18:14] Marcus: Tue works.
[18:18] Asha: works for me.

[18:30] Diego: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with notes and calendar invite.

[18:45] (call ends)

Notes on transcript fidelity: occasional mislabels and dropped punctuation; some technical terms transcribed oddly (e.g., 'KV cache' as 'K V cash') which we've normalized in the notes.
